texts: need a doha about how the stuff we chase looks real but really isnt
Sing of the dazzling world that seems so solid, yet slips away the moment you reach for it.
I keep working for things I assume are permanent, a career, a title, a big impressive life, but lately it all feels staged and hollow. Please write a doha showing how unreal all of this is.
worldly show, nothing real
Spent ten years building a life that looked perfect from outside, and one morning I realised none of it was ever solid.

A tortoise draws its limbs into its shell while the peacock spreads glorious plumes for the world to admire. Please write a doha on how the world's show is unreal and only our attachment keeps us fooled.
doha pls, proud peacock strutting vs a quiet tortoise, about how worldly show isnt real
tortoise, peacock, false show
At the zoo my son laughed at the tortoise ignoring the dancing peacock, and I thought how much of my own life goes into admiring things that are not what they seem.
O peacock, so proud of your painted feathers, and tortoise, calm within your shell: which of you has seen through the world's pretty deceit?

My grandmother sits at her spinning wheel with the sacred mark on her forehead, calmly saying that everything we cling to in this world is only appearance. Please write a doha capturing that quiet knowing about false attachments.
doha about a forehead mark and a spinning wheel, how outward things fool us
The wheel turns and turns, the mark on the brow glows red, and still the world spins its false promises that we take for truth.
spinning wheel, forehead mark, deception
My uncle wears a bright mark on his forehead to every meeting and keeps an old spinning wheel in his lobby for show, yet he is completely hooked on appearances.
A tiny seed dreams of a towering tree, and we too dream of grand lives that are only the stuff of wanting.
I planted a seed in the garden for my daughter and she believes it will become a tree that shades her forever; I wish I could tell her nothing here is quite as it seems.
doha on seed and tree, how what we see isnt the real thing
Everyone treats the seed as a promise and the tree as a fortune, but I wonder if the whole cycle is a trick that keeps us attached to a world that was never truly ours. Write something on that.
tree and seed, worldly deception
false world, real hunger
Beautiful is the world's dream and sweet its fooling; blessed is the soul that wakes and sees it was never there.
Please write me a doha about how everything we call ours, status, belongings, even our plans for tomorrow, only seems real to us, and how seeing through this changes the way we live from day to day.
can u do a couplet, the world looks so convincing but its all pretend
At forty I realised the promotion I fought for over years meant nothing the day I got it, and the thrill faded as if it had never been mine.
Standing at a crossroads, a person holds a needle and wonders which road leads to anything real, since every path in this world promises something that turns out empty. Write a doha on that.
crossroads, needle, false promises
doha about a needle and a crossroads, how the world misleads us
At the crossroads of desire a slender needle can stitch nothing real, for every road is paved with pretty falsehood.
Lost at a crossroads in a new city, I found a needle in my coat pocket from my mother's sewing kit and thought how all my ambitions led nowhere real.
world's false glitter
write a doha, everything we hold dear is not what it seems
My brother bought a huge flat and a fancy car and still looks like he is chasing something that isn't there, and I suspect it never was.

I would like a Kabir-style doha on the way people grow deeply attached to the world's comforts and titles, mistaking passing appearances for something solid and lasting, until the day it all proves hollow.
O seeker, the world's bright pageant is a dream within a dream; wake, and find it never held you.
I keep crossing the same bridge to a job I think will finally make me secure, and I realise the security was never real. Please write a doha about the false comfort of worldly things.
Every morning I cross the bridge to work believing this next goal will make me complete, but the finish line keeps moving.
The bridge arches toward a shore that dissolves as we near it, for the world is a lovely lie.
bridge to nowhere
doha on a bridge that leads nowhere real, like the world
The chakor bird gazes at grains of sand and believes each glint a treasure, just as the heart trusts the world's glitter.
doha pls, chakor bird pecking at sand thinking its something precious
My cousin chases every shiny scheme like a chakor bird after sand, and each time he is sure this one is the answer.
chakor bird, sand, false hope
The chakor bird pecks at sand thinking it is something precious, much as we cling to worldly things that only appear valuable. Compose a doha that shows how deceptive this appearance really is.
On a clear night everyone admires the moon as though its glow were its own, yet the glow is borrowed. Write a doha showing how worldly splendour is the same kind of borrowed show.
I stared at the moon last night after losing my job and thought how the prestige I adored at the old office was only ever borrowed.
doha on the moon and the world's false glow
moon, borrowed glow
The moon pours silver on a sleeping earth; so does the world pour its silver dream upon the sleeping heart.
Sweet is the world's enchantment, yet the heart that trusts it is forever deceived.

Please write a doha for someone who has just realised that the happiness they were chasing in wealth, praise and comfort was never really there, and that the whole pursuit was a kind of sleep they were walking in.
My neighbour spent his whole life polishing a reputation, and at his retirement party nobody remembered what it was for.
can you make a doha about the unreal nature of everything people get attached to
things that seem real, arent

Everybody says the thief steals only what is valuable, but a doha could remind us that the thief and the owner both cling to what is not truly real. Please write it with that gentle, mocking Kabir tone.
The thief runs off with a treasure that was never real, and the owner weeps for it; oh, the world's sweet fooling.
thief, empty prize
A thief broke into our neighbour's home, and watching her cry over her things I wondered why we all give such a deep reality to objects.
doha about a thief and how what he steals isnt even real
Write a doha about how we take an ordinary stone, give it value in our minds, and then become tied to it, forgetting that the value was never there to begin with, only our own wishful seeing.
A friend keeps polishing a large stone from his trip like it will bring him luck, and I can't help thinking we give such meaning to things that are only what we imagine.
stone, false meaning
The stone is carved into a god by hands, and the heart is carved into a believer by habit; ask what is real beneath the shaping.
doha on a stone we treat as precious but its just something we imagine

A long and thoughtful doha, please, about how sandalwood's fragrance and the bitter gourd's plain skin both teach that the outward look of things has little to do with what they truly are, and how we cling to looks.
The sandalwood perfumes the air, the bitter gourd hides its sting; so the world wears fragrance over emptiness.
doha on sandalwood and bitter gourd, looks nice and smells nice but its all show
When I opened the glossy box at the wedding it smelled of sandalwood but held only a bitter gourd's worth of meaning for me.
sandalwood, bitter gourd, outward show
Last year I was sure the big home, the shiny car and the family name would be mine forever, and now I see them as flashes on a screen; I wonder what Kabir would say.
O heart, why do you embrace the glimmer of the world as a dear companion when it fades at the first glance of truth?
Write a doha for me about how everything we think is solid, relationships, wealth, ambitions, is really just a show playing in our minds, and how we suffer by treating it as the real thing.
doha on worldly show pls
unreal attachments
My tongue says I don't care for worldly things, but the lock on my safe tells another story; please write a doha for this contradiction in me.
tongue and lock, doha about words that claim detachment but a heart that holds on
tongue, lock, empty claim
A doha, please, that shows how the tongue can sing about the unreality of the world while the lock of attachment keeps shut on the heart, so we only pretend to see through what still holds us.
The tongue speaks of truth while the lock guards a false treasure; such is the hypocrisy of the world's play.
could u write a doha on how the whole world is a make believe thing we keep believing
Draped in dazzling colours, the world dances before the eyes, and the mind kneels to what its own longing has made.
I would love a doha on the strange human habit of building our entire sense of who we are on things that, if we looked honestly, have no real substance and cannot hold our weight for even a day.
nothing here is real
After my divorce I walked through our old rooms and saw how much of our shared life had been stories we told ourselves.
A drop of dew sits on the grass at dawn like a tiny glass ball, and a seed seems to hold a future; show both as passing appearances the heart mistakes for lasting things.
I told my daughter a tiny seed would grow into everything she dreamed, and a morning dew on the grass later I wondered if I was teaching her to believe in things that vanish.
dew, seed, false promise
The dew shines proud at dawn, the seed swells with dreams, and both are gone before the world has noticed the trick.
doha with dew and seed, about how nothing we hold is as solid as it looks

I spend most weekends chasing purchases I imagine will finally make my life feel complete, and by Tuesday the feeling is gone. Please write a doha on how these things are only promises made by the mind.
Three birthdays running, I bought myself the thing I wanted most, and each time it felt hollow by evening.
appearances that fool us
Beautiful and brittle is the world's pageant; the eye is lured, the hand grasps, and the palm is empty.
doha about being fooled by how real everything seems
lamp, churn, illusion
The lamp burns bright in the hall and the churn turns without end, yet neither brings the truth the heart is seeking.
My mother keeps a lamp lit by the old churn in the corner of her kitchen, and tells me that every comfort of our home is a passing show.

Write a doha where a burning lamp and a butter churn stand for the endless motions of worldly life, which look purposeful and real but only keep us turning and attached to things that are not lasting.
doha pls with a lamp and a churn, about the world not being what it seems

A moth is drawn to a brilliant glow and thinks it has found its heart's desire, only to find the glow was never what it appeared. Please write a doha showing the same trap in our attachment to worldly attractions.
Little moth, why do you dance toward a bright deception that promises everything and keeps nothing?
My friend keeps dating people who look perfect at first and then turn out to be nothing like that, and she walks back into it again like a moth.
doha about a moth and how shiny things trick us
moth, deceptive glow

When my grandmother threads a needle she says the world is like the eye of it, a tiny gap that looks wide and inviting but cannot hold anything real. Write a doha built on that thought about worldly show.
couplet on a needle and how the world isnt what it looks
I spent a week hunting for a single needle in a heap of old clothes and caught myself thinking how often we hunt for things that were never worth the search.
needle, hollow world
Slender needle, sharp little teacher, you pierce the veil of the world's bright garment and show the nothing it hides.

A crow struts about the courtyard believing everything it sees is its own to claim, while the world quietly plays its tricks. Please write a doha about how the things we think we own are only appearances.
The crow croaks at the world's passing parade, certain each glittering scrap is its own, as we are certain of ours.
doha on a crow calling stuff its own, how worldly things deceive
A crow keeps stealing shiny things from my balcony, and I realised I do the same with every thing that catches my eye in life.
crow, false treasures

Every festival my family puts a bright mark on the forehead as a sign of devotion, but I notice that many people wear the mark more for appearance than for truth. Write a doha on the world's love of show.
At my cousin's wedding everybody wore a mark on the forehead and a smile, and I couldn't tell which of the two was real.
forehead mark, outward show
doha on a forehead mark and how outer show fools us
The mark on the brow is red and fine, yet the heart behind it wanders far; how clever the world is at dressing up nothing.
door, thorn, deception
Behind a beautiful door a thorn waits for the hand that reaches in eagerly, and in the same way the world offers pleasure while hiding the hurt. Write a doha about this deceit of appearances.
The door of the new flat looked so promising until the first month's bills pricked me like a thorn, and I realised how much I'd believed the pretty picture.
doha on a door and a thorn, about the world's fake promise
Open the door of the world and a thorn lies waiting under its petals, for every sweetness there is bait.
write a doha on the tortoise and the yogi, how they both see past the worlds show
My yoga teacher, who moves slowly like a tortoise, once said that all we call real is mostly a story we keep telling; I'd love a doha on that.
The tortoise withdraws, the yogi closes his eyes, and both see the world's glitter for what it is, a passing dream.
tortoise, yogi, unreal world

Please compose a doha showing a yogi and a tortoise withdrawing from the senses and recognising that the things people cling to in the world are not what they appear, and how that vision frees the heart.
The thief creeps in under cover of night to steal a treasure that is itself only a dream of the owner.
Write a doha on how the thief steals things we thought were permanent and shows us, by taking them away, that we had only imagined them to be ours and real in the first place.
When my bike was stolen outside the station, I felt less angry than oddly relieved, as if I'd seen how little the thing had really been mine.
doha with a thief in it, about how things we think we own are just pretend
thief, unreal ownership
The sand slips through the fingers however tightly the hand is closed, and so the things we cling to in life vanish even as we hold them. Write a doha about the unreal grip of worldly attachment.
I spent years building a business that now feels like sand in my hand, every grain slipping away as I tighten my fist.
doha on sand and how nothing we hold is real
Fine sand in the hand of the child is a kingdom; open the hand, and the kingdom is gone.
sand, empty grasp
The pearl glows in its shell, yet who can say whether its beauty is a gift or a dream the mind has dressed up?
Please write a doha about a pearl that people prize so highly, and how our whole sense of its worth is a kind of agreement that has little to do with what is truly real or lasting in life.
My aunt wore her pearl necklace to every function, and when it broke, she laughed and said it was only ever our belief that held it together.
doha about a pearl that looks precious but its just our idea
pearl, imagined worth
the world's grand pretence
All my life I dressed to impress and spoke to be praised, and at fifty-five I find I do not know who was behind all that.
Write a doha that gently reminds a reader how the pleasures, titles and possessions of ordinary life seem so firm and real, but once you look into them with a quiet mind they dissolve into nothing.
need a doha, kinda about how nothing we cling to is real
Oh heart, wake from the sweet sleep of the world's glamour, for none of what you embrace there has ever had a body.
A cloud drifts across the sky looking like a mighty fortress, then breaks apart in the wind; I want a doha that says worldly splendour is just that kind of passing shape that deceives us.
cloud, shapes that deceive
doha about a cloud that looks solid but isnt, like everything we hold
I used to think my career was a fortress, but it turned out more like a cloud and floated off once the company restructured.
Proud cloud, you build a kingdom of vapour in the sky, and the wind laughs, as the world laughs at those who trust its shapes.
thread, dew, fragile appearance
Mom keeps one loose thread from my childhood shirt, and this morning, looking at dew on her window, I felt how everything we cling to is as thin and temporary.
Write a doha on how a single thread and a drop of dew both look so real and tangible, yet the slightest touch undoes them, just like the worldly things we are so attached to.
The thread is spun so fine, the dew so bright, and both undo themselves before the day has climbed; so fades the world we love.
doha with a thread and dew in it, how the world seems real but vanishes
doha on a net and salt, how the world catches us with things that arent real
My brother got caught in a get-rich scheme that tasted sweet at first and then turned salty, and now he sits tangled in a net of debt.
The net is cast over a crowd of sweet appearances, and the salt of truth stings only the one who wakes inside it.
Please compose a doha about a net spread by the world's temptations, and salt that tastes of truth, to show how we are caught by false appearances and only realise it when the bitterness arrives.
net, salt, trapped by appearances
I woke up at three in the morning realising the life I had worked so hard to build was something I'd been performing for others, not living.

Please write a doha about the way worldly attachment makes us confuse our titles, belongings and reputations with who we truly are, though none of that has any substance when examined with honest eyes.
can i get a doha on how nothing in this world is what it looks like
all appearance, no substance
How beautifully the world pretends, and how sweetly we agree to be fooled, again and again, by what was never there.
write something on how people mistake the world for the real thing

A seeker once told me that most suffering comes from believing the world is solid and lasting when it is only a passing display. Please write a doha that shows this clearly and gently without sounding too harsh.
Everyone in my family fought over the inheritance as if it were something eternal, and I just sat there thinking how all of it is borrowed.
mistaken for real
Like a traveling show of sweet sounds and colours, the world arrives, enchants the crowd, and leaves before the truth is told.
The cuckoo calls across the shore and the ocean answers, and both are sweet illusions the mind takes to be home.
doha pls, cuckoo singing by the ocean, how worldly beauty fools us

Write a doha about the cuckoo's sweet song and the vast ocean, showing how the beauty and magnitude of the world can hypnotise the heart into believing it is lasting, when in truth it is only passing.
On our last holiday by the ocean a cuckoo sang every morning and I felt such perfect happiness that I knew, even then, it was a feeling that wouldn't stay.
cuckoo, ocean, fleeting beauty
not what it seems
I would like a doha for a friend who keeps pouring his energy into impressing people and acquiring things, and who has not yet seen that none of it has real weight or stays with him.
write me a doha about how worldly stuff is just pretend
My sister cried when she lost her phone, her contacts and photos, and later laughed, saying we are all so attached to things that don't even exist in the hand.
Beautiful is the world's fiction, and tender the heart that believes it, yet truth waits beyond the story.
cotton, soft deception

Cotton looks light and soft like a puff of comfort, but those who rest their whole life upon it find it blows away at the smallest wind. Write a doha about how worldly comforts deceive in the same way.
I bought a mattress filled with the softest cotton and paid more for the feeling of security than for sleep, and I still lie awake.
Soft cotton, you promise a pillow for the weary head, yet you are only dust of the field in the guise of comfort.
doha about cotton and how comfy things are a trick
At my uncle's workshop the furnace roars all day, and he comes home with a mark on his forehead and a heart full of schemes, forever busy with things that don't last.
The furnace glows and the mark on the brow shines; both are the world's way of dressing up the ordinary as holy.

Please write a doha where the roaring furnace stands for the world's endless busyness and the mark on the forehead for outward show, together showing how little of it is real or worth the heart's attachment.
doha on a forehead mark and a furnace, worldly show vs whats real
furnace, forehead mark, hollow show
Last night I lay under the stars while a bell in the distance rang, and everything I'd been so anxious about at work felt suddenly unreal.

Write a doha where the countless stars above and the ringing of a bell remind us that the busy, important-looking things of our days are not as real or lasting as we believe, and clinging is a mistake.
doha with stars and a bell, about how the worlds worries arent real
The bell rings in the dark, the stars look down in silence, and the world's solid-seeming dreams grow thin as breath.
stars, bell, unreal worries
need a doha on the philosopher's stone and the stars, how chasing them is chasing an illusion

Alchemists once searched for the philosopher's stone and sailors studied the stars, yet both pursuits can become a kind of attachment to something unreachable. Write a doha about the false hope hidden in such seeking.
philosopher's stone, starry lure
My father spent his life hunting for the one big break, the philosopher's stone of his business, and died still looking up at the stars of his ambition.
The philosopher's stone gleams in the mind's night, the stars wink from their far homes, and the seeker follows both into nothing.
The pearl in the oyster, the philosopher's stone in legend, both shine in the mind's night, and neither is held by one who clings.
doha pls, pearl and philosopher's stone, about chasing treasures that arent real

Please write a doha about the pearl that men dive for and the philosopher's stone that men dream of, showing how both are objects of attachment that promise riches and never deliver peace or anything lasting.
My cousin spent his savings on an investment that promised to turn everything he had into a pearl, and now he talks about it like a philosopher's stone he never found.
pearl, philosopher's stone, false treasure
Every night I scroll through other people's perfect lives and every morning I feel hollow, though I know at some level none of it is real.
I would like a doha that shows how everyday attachment to image, comfort and approval builds a kind of dream-world around us, and how the wise gently step out of it without anger or pride.
pls write a doha on the false stuff the world keeps selling us
Oh brief and brilliant world, your promises are written on nothing, and your colours fade at the first dawn of truth.
everything looks real, isn't
doha about a tortoise sitting on a stone and the worlds fake promises
tortoise, stone, quiet truth
Every evening an old tortoise sits on the stone by our gate, unbothered by the noisy street, and I envy that it does not mistake any of it for real.

A tortoise rests on a stone without any sense of owning it or being owned by the world around it. Write a doha that contrasts this calm with human attachment to a world that only seems solid and lasting.
The tortoise on the stone has seen a thousand sunrises and trusts none of the world's bright claims.
false world, wake up

Compose a doha for someone who feels that the life they chose, the possessions and the praise, seems less real every year, and who wants to understand why something so firm to the touch can feel like nothing.
pls doha: world looks so real but its not
When my father sold the family land, the deeds we fought over suddenly looked like papers with ink, and I stood staring at them for a long time.
Thin as breath is the world's painted splendour, though the hands that grasp it feel certainty in their grip.
write a doha, how things only seem real until you look closely
I once held a stack of cash in my hands and felt strangely nothing, as if I had been tricked about what it could give me.
seeming, not being
Dear heart, the world's bright show has ended, and behind it there is nothing at all to cling to.

Please write a doha for a retired person who has spent forty years chasing titles and savings and now sits quietly noticing that what seemed so important was never quite as real as it looked from within.
Write a doha telling someone anxious about losing status and possessions that what they fear losing was never as real or lasting as it looked, and that the fear belongs to the same false picture.
unreal and unreliable
A chess champion told me that after winning everything he felt like the pieces had never mattered, and I thought of my own long chase.
The scene fades when the truth is lifted high; the world was only ever a story told in colour.
tell me a doha about how the worlds a fake out
The ferry boat I take across to work every morning feels like a small world of its own, and I notice we all pretend the journey matters more than it does.
The boat drifts upon waters of seeming, and each passenger holds tight to a shore that does not exist.
doha about a boat that goes nowhere, like the worlds fake promises
boat, shoreless voyage

Please write a doha where a boat sails across wide waters and everything on board, wealth and rank included, is only appearance, so that the voyage becomes a picture of life lived in attachment to what is not real.
At my grandmother's funeral I watched everyone bow before the bier, then rush back to their phones and deals, and I wondered which of the two things was real.
bier, traveler, passing show
doha on a traveler and a bier, how the worlds attachments are fake
The traveler rests a night beside the bier and dreams the road ahead is his; at dawn the dream, like the world, has gone.

Write a doha where a traveler passes a bier on his way and still keeps planning tomorrow's gains, showing how deeply worldly attachment fools the mind into believing that this scene is real and lasting.
seed, gold, false promise
doha about a seed and gold, how the things we chase arent real

A farmer buries a seed hoping it will turn into gold, and the world feeds on exactly that hope, promising wealth while giving shadows. Write a doha about how this hope keeps us bound to what is not real.
In the dark earth a seed dreams itself into gold, and the dreamer wakes with only soil beneath his fingers.
My uncle put his entire savings into a scheme that promised to turn a small seed of money into gold, and he still believes in it.
